title: The realization-singular counit is a weak homotopy equivalence
statement: Use simplicial sets, geometric realization and the homotopy groups $\pi_r(-,t)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe large enough for the sets of continuous maps below. For a topological space $T$ let $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$, with operators given by precomposition with the affine maps $|\alpha|$ of topological simplices. The evaluation map $$\varepsilon_T:|\operatorname{Sing}(T)|\to T,\qquad [\sigma,s]\mapsto\sigma(s)\quad(\sigma\in\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n,\ s\in|\Delta^n|),$$ is well defined, continuous and natural in continuous maps $T\to T'$. It induces a bijection from the path components of $|\operatorname{Sing}(T)|$ to those of $T$, and for every $r\geq1$ and every point $x\in|\operatorname{Sing}(T)|$ an isomorphism $\pi_r(|\operatorname{Sing}(T)|,x)\to\pi_r(T,\varepsilon_T(x))$, where $\pi_r(T,y)$ denotes homotopy classes relative to the boundary of continuous maps $([0,1]^r,\partial[0,1]^r)\to(T,y)$. No Hausdorff, compact generation, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption on $T$ is imposed.
